message.content:
For each integer \(k\) from \(1\) to \(12\), \(k\) is nonzero modulo \(13\), so it has a unique inverse modulo \(13\).

The mapping
\[
k \mapsto k^{-1} \pmod{13}
\]
is a permutation of the nonzero residues \(1,2,\dots,12\). Therefore, the set of inverses is exactly the same set \(\{1,2,\dots,12\}\).

So the sum is
\[
1+2+\cdots+12 = \frac{12\cdot 13}{2}=78.
\]
Modulo \(13\),
\[
78 \equiv 0 \pmod{13}.
\]

The answer is 0.
